extracted.intended_audience: federal grant-making agencies and grants management officials (and stakeholders implementing OMB grant policy)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory implementation actions from OMB to federal grant-making agencies on grants policy, systems, forms, reporting, and procedures. Includes timelines, required changes to agency practice, and directives intended to reduce burden or improve grants management.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrating New Data Standards (M-18-24)
rubrics_metrics.description: By September 30, 2018, government-wide core grants management data standards are expected to be finalized by the Grants Management Federal Integrated Business Framework (FIBF). By April 30, 2019, agencies must submit a plan to OMB that describes their strategy for integrating the new data standards into current and/or future grant systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must finalize and then plan integration of the new government-wide core grants management data standards; plans are due to OMB by April 30, 2019. This is part of implementing lessons from the DATA Act to reduce reporting burden and standardize grants data.

rubrics_metrics.name: SF-424B Form Phase-Out (M-18-24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 1, 2019, the SF-424B will become optional and agencies shall make plans to phase out its use in Funding Opportunity Announcements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must stop requiring SF-424B as of 1/1/2019 and update FOAs / processes to remove reliance on SF-424B, documenting phase-out plans where appropriate to reduce applicant burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralize Certifications and Representations via SAM (M-18-24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective January 1, 2020, SAM.gov will become the central repository for common government-wide certifications and representations required of Federal grants recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal agencies must use SAM information to comply with award requirements and to avoid separate requests for the same certifications and representations, reducing duplicative data collection and recipient burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sharing of Systems and Services to Reduce Legacy Burden (M-18-24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are to work with other agencies and OMB to reduce the number of existing legacy systems and grants recipient burden via sharing quality services and systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote inter-agency sharing of grants management systems/services to lower costs and simplify recipient interactions rather than maintaining disparate legacy systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Increase Micro-Purchase and Simplified Acquisition Thresholds (M-18-18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Micro-purchase threshold for federal financial assistance awards increased to $10,000; threshold for simplified acquisitions increased to $250,000 for all recipients.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal awarding agencies are required to implement these threshold changes in award terms and conditions. Recipients of existing awards may implement the new thresholds in their internal controls; agencies must update award language accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescind/Modify Certain Grants-Related OMB Memoranda to Reduce Burden (M-17-26)
rubrics_metrics.description: M-17-26 identified and eliminated various federal regulations and rescinded or modified prior OMB memoranda to reduce burdens on federal agencies related to grants management.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This memorandum instructs agencies that a set of prior requirements (including aspects of M-14-17 and M-12-01) are eliminated or modified; agencies should follow M-17-26's list of rescissions/modifications to reduce administrative burdens.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Longer Required to Report Metrics Measuring Uniform Guidance Impact (M-17-26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are no longer required to report the metrics measuring the impact of the Uniform Guidance (2 C.F.R. Part 200) as instructed earlier by OMB Memorandum M-14-17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove or discontinue reporting processes and requirements tied to M-14-17 metrics unless otherwise directed; update internal reporting expectations to reflect this change.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disbandment of COFAR; CFO Council to Consider Financial Assistance Priorities (M-17-26)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Council on Financial Assistance Reform (COFAR) is disbanded. Moving forward, financial assistance priorities will be considered by the Chief Financial Officers (CFO) Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should shift participation and coordination on financial assistance priorities from COFAR to the CFO Council and adjust governance and stakeholder engagement accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metrics for Uniform Guidance (M-14-17)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OMB summarizes major reforms in the Uniform Guidance and outlines metrics that will help the government gauge their effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies were provided a metrics framework to assess the effectiveness of Uniform Guidance reforms; although later reporting requirements were altered by M-17-26, the metrics framework itself is documented in M-14-17 for assessing implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return to Normal Grants.gov Operations (M-10-16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Federal grant-making agencies that began using alternative methods to collect applications during the Recovery Act period are instructed to resume their normal use of Grants.gov's Find and Apply functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should stop using temporary alternative application collection methods and restore standard Grants.gov application channels to improve consistency and centralization of FOAs and application submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agencies to Help Cover Costs to Improve Grants.gov (M-09-17)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB asked federal grant-making agencies to help cover costs required to improve Grants.gov amid Recovery Act implementation due to a large influx of additional applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies should contribute resources/support as needed to establish a more efficient, flexible, and reliable Grants.gov system to handle increased workload.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan for Grants.gov Improvements and Alternative Application Methods (M-09-14)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB instructed HHS and GSA to develop a plan to improve Grants.gov given Recovery Act application volume, and asked agencies to prepare to accept applications via temporary, alternative methods in case Grants.gov is unavailable during critical periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must coordinate with HHS/GSA on improvement plans and maintain contingency application collection methods for critical periods to avoid disruptions in application intake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect DUNS Numbers for All Financial Assistance (M-08-19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies are instructed to collect Dun & Bradstreet Data Universal Numbering System (DUNS) numbers in applications for all types of financial assistance subject to the Federal Funding Accountability and Transparency Act of 2006.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all application processes capture DUNS numbers for covered awards to comply with the Transparency Act; this extended prior narrower DUNS collection requirements to all financial assistance types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate Funds to Migrate Existing Grant Management Systems to Grants.gov (M-04-05)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB clarifies that federal grant-making agencies should designate funds to cover the cost of migrating existing grant management systems to Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must budget for migration costs and prioritize transitioning internal systems to integrate with or announce FOAs through Grants.gov as the centralized platform.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publish Funding Opportunity Announcements on Grants.gov (M-04-01)
rubrics_metrics.description: OMB directs all federal grant-making agencies to publish funding opportunity announcements (synopses) on Grants.gov to allow the public to identify funding opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must use Grants.gov to post FOAs/synopses as part of implementing the Federal Financial Assistance Management Improvement Act; this centralizes public access to opportunities.
